answer: A plume of new identities is cheap to spawn, so an agent economy should require each account to stake a refundable deposit before it can transact at the summit of the marketplace. The stake is locked in a haven contract and slashed if the account is caught attesting its own work or running duplicate identities. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest from fees, while a sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so the cost of forging a thousand identities grows linearly and quickly exceeds any reward from gaming the system.
